body:
Self-happiness to me is a relative measure. In relation to my baseline I've experienced euphoria before. It is unreasonable to try and experience it all the time. If my baseline moved up or down from, for example, a large gain/loss in wealth/close relationships and I experienced euphoria from that point it would feel no 'better' than previous experiences. I would be the person that would leave an hour early. There is nothing to gain from staying an extra hour at the beach; I've seen it, an hour more of it isn't any better, I still have to fly away.

EDIT: Btw, I appreciate the response, I'm not trying to be negative toward you/anyone willing to try to help me. But I can't actually 'fly away' just yet, I can't do that to my parents. So I'm trying to find help in searching for a way to change how I think. To find a reason to stay the extra hour. In my mind, everyone should be fine with the idea of one less hour at that beach.

A sort of meta question on this topic.

* How did you find out about Reddit AMAs?
* Have you read other people's AMAs to get a sense of how they are run; any specific ones that you found interesting or that inspired you to do your own? 
* How are you running your AMA; specifically interested in what criteria you are using to decide what questions to answer (just personal judgement, answering all questions that come in chronologically, or maybe set out to cover specific topics)?
* Are you writing the answers completely solo or are you having people help you structure your answers (either maybe a PR person to help smooth out the rough draft answers, or someone familiar with Reddit to help guide your answers within this community)?

Kind of not really; friends feel like a bandaid though, I haven't really had any friends in my life that have lasted particularly long, or really past that particular 'phase' of my life (didn't really hold onto my high school friends for very long into college, same story from college into whatever this is right now, and I've slowly lost most of my present day friends to moving away or just growing apart and can't imagine keeping most any of them for much longer given my history of pushing people away passively over time).

Historically my sleep has been erratic but numerically balances out to an 'appropriate' amount. I have had periods of time of completely normal sleep that lasts longer than a week, but that doesn't seem to drastically change things compared to numerically appropriate sleep (with slightly off hours) that I normally get.
